title: Rappolo disappears in Minneapolis
summary: Rappolo, mistaken for a burglar, goes missing and is found eating bananas; Marigold Ballroom 1924.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And the fella's description tallied with Rap. Although I know Rap didn't do it because Rap was working with us. He couldn't have done it. So one night Rap don't show up. He comes up missing and everybody's wondering. He got a hold of his wife and said, I don't know where he is. He went to work and all this. So I got a hold of the police department and told them that Rap would answer to the description of this guy almost. And I said, I think he's lost his memory. They had a lapse of memory. And I said, if you see him, don't shoot him. Just pick him up. And I said, my name and address and telephone. If you call me, I'll come down and identify him first. So they finally caught him. He was in a grocery store, combination grocery and fruit. He was eating bananas, picking them off the stalk. So the banana people, the man that owned the place, he didn't know who Rap was. But he had read the description of the burglar, highwayman. And one day The only trouble though, you see, he hopped one of his clarinets for a pistol. And he had that pistol in his pocket. And we had an awful lot of talking to do to get him squared up. Of course, it was easy when we got the manager of the ballroom to go down in McCluskey.
He testified he was playing. He went down, sure.
He went down to the police station and, well, he's a well-known man around town anyhow. And I think that possibly he's...
That was in Minneapolis? Yes. What year? Do you remember?
Well, no. I can't just say offhand what year it was.

No. Later than that? Yeah, that was about 30... Oh, I'd say 38. Maybe 39. About that time. It'd be about that time. Uh... No, on second thought, I'm pretty positive it was in the fall of 1924. Or possibly 25, but I'm pretty positive it was in 1924 that we were in Minneapolis.
Do you remember the name of the place where you played up there?
We played the Marigold Ballroom. Uh-huh.
